patches.reason: Remove a still-free block from its free tree before coalescing during allocation-failure rollback. Otherwise a range-split OOM leaves freed metadata in the tree; scripts/test-gpu-buddy.sh reproduces it as an ASan negative control. AMDGPU driver sources are unchanged.

verified_copies.reason: Shadow headers in linuxu/headers that are byte-identical to the pinned upstream file. They stay in the shim include tree because <linux/...>, <drm/...> and <uapi/...> must resolve there without adding the upstream include/ directory to the search path; the verifier checks each one against the submodule.

compile_interventions.reason: Routes only the GFX12 GART placement call through the host-window policy so GART lands on the client-reserved host VA without overlapping VRAM. amdgpu_gmc.c keeps the original symbol.

compile_interventions.scope: every DriverKit upstream and linuxu object
compile_interventions.reason: Replaces memset/memcpy/memmove/memcmp/bzero with scalar volatile routines. Compiler-generated DC ZVA and vector stores fault on BAR0 device memory.

config_interventions.reason: Kconfig selects DRM_AMD_DC_FP only when ARCH_HAS_KERNEL_FPU_SUPPORT && !(CC_IS_CLANG && ARM64), because arm64 kernel code is built with -mgeneral-regs-only and clang cannot confine FP use to the kernel_fpu_begin()/kernel_fpu_end() sections. linuxu builds the DCN, DML and DML2 objects as ordinary userspace code: the FP/SIMD registers are always usable and preserved by the OS across context switches, kernel_fpu_begin()/kernel_fpu_end() (linuxu/headers/linux/fpu.h) track the section per task, and dc_fpu.c's per-CPU recursion depth is per task (linuxu/headers/linux/percpu.h). Without it every DCN (dcn10 and later, including DCN 4.0.1) is compiled out and amdgpu_dm cannot create a DC instance for any RDNA GPU.

mesa.reason: Mesa's RADV Vulkan driver for macOS (scripts/build-radv.sh), on the upstream amdgpu DRM interface through libdrm-mlg. Fetched only for the Vulkan build: scripts/bootstrap.sh --with-mesa or --mesa-only.

patches.reason: Build wiring for macOS: find libdrm through pkg-config on Darwin when RADV is built (Mesa only looks for it on kernel-DRM systems), select addrlib's portable type definitions (HAVE_TSERVER) instead of the Apple kernel driver's private header, and link RADV with -undefined dynamic_lookup as KosmicKrisp does, because Mach-O cannot leave the entrypoint tables' weak layer symbols undefined.

RADV opens and stats render nodes, maps buffers and issues requests with the system calls, which cannot reach a driver outside the kernel. When libdrm defines LIBDRM_FILE_OPS (libdrm-mlg), util/os_drm.h routes ioctl through drmIoctl and new os_drm_open/stat/mmap/munmap wrappers through libdrm's drmFile* functions; RADV's six call sites use the wrappers. Without LIBDRM_FILE_OPS nothing changes.

Apple silicon maps PCIe BARs for the CPU as Device memory only, so memcpy into a CPU mapping of VRAM faults on unaligned stores (seen on the R9700: SIGBUS creating the device). On Apple silicon the winsys reports no CPU-visible VRAM and places any buffer that is not NO_CPU_ACCESS in GTT, whose mappings are normal memory. Without CPU-visible VRAM, shader code is uploaded by SDMA into VRAM (NO_CPU_ACCESS arenas) instead of being fetched from GTT.

RADV presents Metal surfaces through the GPU's own display engine: VK_EXT_metal_surface on the macOS platform, and for a driver that is neither software nor Metal a swapchain whose images are framebuffers of the GPU's primary node shown on the driver's display output (libdrm-mlg's drmMlgScanout), on the primary plane or on an overlay plane at the window's rectangle, with no copy. MLG_WSI_OUTPUT names the output; without it the surface reports no presentation support. Other drivers are unchanged.

llama_cpp.reason: llama.cpp, the first application of the Vulkan path: its Vulkan backend on RADV (scripts/build-llama-vulkan.sh). Fetched only for that build: scripts/bootstrap.sh --llama-only. Patched as declared below.

patches.reason: Every request to the GPU is a round trip to the driver process (about 100 us for a trivial request on the R9700), so Vulkan's per-token synchronous work dominates decode. The scheduler wrote each graph input with a blocking set_tensor (a queue submission, a fence wait and a reset on a device without host-visible VRAM, as on Apple silicon), and ggml_vk_synchronize signalled its fence with an empty submission, which RADV turns into eight syncobj requests when it also waits for the transfer queue. Inputs are now staged in host memory and copied in the compute stream (a new optional backend function the scheduler uses for user inputs), the fence goes with the last compute submission, transfer-only work is waited for on the host, and a host copy uses the transfer queue only above a per-device size measured on first use (submission overhead times host-to-device bandwidth). test-backend-sched-inputs covers input capture and ordering.
